options.text: Heated land warms moist air; rising air creates low pressure; cooler air flows in, rises, cools, and water vapour condenses into storm clouds and rain.
Storm clouds and rain form by the same chain even if the air above the land is dry.
Dark storm clouds alone prove the heating-and-rising chain has already finished, with no need to check moist air or pressure.
Cool surrounding air must stay still; inflow into the low-pressure area is not part of the storm chain.

stem:
Ayesha feels hot, moist air over sun-heated land just before a thunderstorm forms.

Which claim correctly describes the chain that produces the thunderstorm?

teacher.key_rationale: Thunderstorms follow heated land warming moist air, rising that creates low pressure, inflow of cooler air, further rising and cooling, and condensation into clouds and rain. Dry air omits a needed condition; dark clouds alone are a surface cue; blocking inflow mis-scopes the chain.
